# PRD 002: Search

**Schema**: pij/prd · **Source**: 002-search.dd.json · **Sections**: 8

## Meta

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| title | PRD 002: Search |
| status | draft |
| updated | 2026-11-16 |
| owner | project lead |
| summary | Search is how an agent or the operator gets from loose words to the right nodes in a graph. This PRD describes the whole feature as it should be, not a change to it: one command that finds nodes by exact value, by words and by meaning, says how and how strongly each was found, and gives the caller enough in one reply to judge the hits and take the next step. Each row is the desired state. A row is `shipped` when umx behaves that way today, and `planned` or `in-progress` when it does not yet; its note says which part is missing. When search changes, the row that describes that behaviour is rewritten here, so this document always reads as the feature. |

<a id="why"></a>

## Why

An agent using a graph starts almost every task by searching it. The agent is a capable model, so it is the judge of what is relevant: search does not need to be clever on its behalf, it needs to hand over what the agent needs to judge quickly. Today a search hit gives an id, a type, a title and scoring numbers. It gives none of the node's text, none of its links and no hints, so the agent spends more calls opening hits than searching.

A review on a private graph of 536 nodes (2026-11-16) also showed that what gets embedded matters more than how it is ranked. Label fields with three distinct values held 29% of the graph's vectors. A search for one label value returned eight rows with the same score, and 92% of each node's nearest neighbours by meaning shared its label (34% by chance). Each of those vectors was an embedder call that made search worse. Inside one graph the calibrated floor cut almost nothing: 55% of all node pairs scored above it, because everything in a graph is on the same subject.

Meaning and structure do different jobs. An embedding says two things are near each other; it cannot say how they are related. The graph's typed links say exactly that. So search by meaning is the way in, and the links are how the caller moves on. This PRD keeps both in one reply.

The project lead ruled three things on 2026-11-16: only prose is embedded (a custom string field is data unless declared content); no second model is added to umx (no reranker); and the tooling is tuned so agents need fewer calls.

<a id="actors"></a>

## Actors

| id | name | need |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a-agent | external agent | Find the right nodes for a loosely worded question in one call, judge them without opening each one, and know the next command to run. |
| a-operator | the operator | Search graphs from the UI with the same results an agent gets, and trust that labels and ids are found exactly. |
| a-builder | graph-building agent | Know which fields are searched by meaning and be told when a field is in the wrong group. |

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

| id | goal |
| --- | --- |
| g-1 | One search call returns hits an agent can judge and act on without a follow-up read for each hit. |
| g-2 | Every hit says how it was found and how strong it is; everything left out or weak is said in a hint with the command to run next. |
| g-3 | Only prose is searched by meaning. Labels, ids, names and times are found exactly and never cost an embedder call. |
| g-4 | The same graphs and query give the same list on every machine. |
| g-5 | Search works, and says what is missing, when there is no embedder. |

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non goals

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| ng-1 | A reranker or any second model inside umx. The calling agent is the judge (project lead, 2026-11-16). The one embedder stays. |
| ng-2 | An approximate vector index. Every vector search is an exact scan, which is fast enough at the sizes graphs reach. |
| ng-3 | A vector per word (late interaction). It multiplies storage about 50 times in files that are committed to git. |
| ng-4 | Embeddings trained on the graph's links. Graphs have too few links for it today. |
| ng-5 | Typo tolerance and phrase search in `umx search`. `umx node find` tolerates typos in titles. |
| ng-6 | Embedder providers, where vectors are stored, secured-graph rules, floors and their calibration, and the similarity verbs (similar_to, similarity pairs, most like this set). Those stay in PRD 001 until they have a feature PRD of their own; this PRD names them only where search depends on them. |

| search-01 | One list from three ways of finding | `umx search &lt;words&gt;` finds nodes three ways and returns one ranked list. Words: the query's words appear in the title, the note or a string field, ranked so a rare word counts for more than a common one and a title match for more than a note match. Meaning: the node's vectors are close to the query's, so a paraphrase with none of the node's words can find it. Exact hits come first; words and meaning are fused by rank.
